purpose: The committed ceiling on explicit deferral. Nothing prevented a stream from adding a deferred route or scenario; 49/21 had been stable by convention alone. Three rules in `graph verify` read this file: `route-deferral-regression` and `scenario-deferral-regression` fail an id that is deferred and not named here, so adding a deferral needs an explicit bump in the same commit and becomes a reviewed decision instead of a diff nobody reads; `deferral-irreversible` fails an id listed in `retired`, so an id that has once left the floor can never come back as architecture debt. The ratchet is monotone non-increasing, not strictly decreasing: requiring the number to fall every release manufactures pressure to mount a route badly to make a number move.
regenerate: This file is committed and hand-edited, unlike `release/test-registry.json`. An id enters `routes` or `scenarios` only with the change that defers it, and leaves only with the change that mounts, deletes or un-defers it - moving it to `retired` in the same commit unless the contract deletes it outright.

routes.floorNote: The approved ceiling remains 48. Human approval is deleted from the Bash MVP contract rather than deferred: Bash auto-approves, and interactive approval policy is recorded in the backlog. Session creation, message admission, exact-generation live files, cancellation, lifecycle, deletion, and telemetry exports are mounted with their production authorities. Deleted persistence, trash/restore, generic-secret, typed skill/tool/instruction/MCP, public run, and approval routes do not count as deferrals.

scenarios.floorNote: Eight deployed public user journeys plus the hosted files companion now own billing, message streaming, terminal retention, telemetry, provider matrix, MCP, storage, long-context, and file evidence. Seven broader lifecycle/fault journeys remain explicit gaps.
